- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 30d forecasts.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast increase to +3–5% above peak.
- If supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates (≥0.67), model underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% downward adjustment to forecast mean.
- When official events are frequent (≥15 events/30d) and supply net is negative, model tends to lag in recognizing downward pressure; shift forecast downward by 1–4% relative to prior 7d average.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply 1–3% downward adjustment to forecast mean if price has been rising for 5+ days.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, model tends to overreact to recent highs; use 3–5 day moving average of true prices as anchor for correction.
